Article Title: 'You might want to explain. Unless, you want me to': Rahul Gandhi's cryptic post over Rubio's Mumbai visit
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi takes a swipe at PM Narendra Modi over US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s upcoming Mumbai visit, alleging confusion within the external affairs ministry over the meeting

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Friday questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi over US secretary of state Marco Rubio ’s upcoming Mumbai visit, alleging that officials in the external affairs ministry were "confused" about the developments.“Mr Rubio has summoned his employee to Mumbai. Modi ji, your officials in the external affairs ministry are confused about what's going on. You might want to explain. Unless, of course, you want me to,” Rahul posted on X.His remarks came a day after Congress questioned the Centre’s silence on Rubio’s visit, particularly after US ambassador to India Sergio Gor said American officials expected external affairs minister S Jaishankar to meet Rubio in Mumbai.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh called the ambassador’s statement “extraordinary” and questioned why the announcement of the external affairs minister’s engagements in India was coming from a US official rather than the ministry of external affairs (MEA).“Why is the MEA silent on the external affairs minister's tryst with Mr Rubio in Mumbai?” Ramesh asked, adding that India was learning about the developments from the US ambassador.The US state department announced on Tuesday that Rubio would visit India from October 17 to 22 to strengthen energy cooperation. He is scheduled to travel to Mumbai and Jamnagar after visiting Samarkand in Uzbekistan.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notices to Rahul Gandhi , Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and other protestors over their October 12 march to the apex court to protest alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The bench, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and comprising Justice Joymalya Bagchi, said issuing notice on the petition did not mean it was condoning the conduct of the political leaders during the march.ALSO READ: Imran Khan asked to leave India: What rights do OCI cardholders have? “We will issue notice but we want to know his conduct on the next date of hearing,” the CJI said, referring to Rahul.During the hearing, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said, “We are not sitting in ivory towers, we are aware of statements made outside the Court” after lawyers referred to attempts to “browbeat” the judiciary through the march. The CJI said the court would ask Rahul to explain how crowds entered the Supreme Court premises during the demonstration.The INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli – March for Democracy’, led by Rahul, brought thousands of supporters into central Delhi on October 12. The opposition was demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and a halt to the SIR exercise over alleged electoral irregularities.The march saw supporters gather along roads between Connaught Place and the Supreme Court, waving party flags and raising slogans.Police stopped the procession near Barakhamba Road, where some demonstrators pushed through barricades as security personnel attempted to hold them back. The crowd later gathered along Bhagwan Das Road, with some supporters climbing onto parked police vehicles and buses.Rahul was joined by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Akhilesh Yadav, RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav and other INDIA bloc leaders. The procession followed the CJI’s refusal to meet opposition representatives seeking to submit a memorandum on alleged electoral irregularities. He had advised them to file a formal petition, citing matters already pending before the court.The opposition’s separate petition challenging the SIR process alleges arbitrary voter deletions and seeks greater transparency and safeguards in the revision of electoral rolls. The Supreme Court also issued notice to the Election Commission of India on that plea.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notices to Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and other protestors over their October 12 march to the apex court. The bench, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and comprising Justice Joymalya Bagchi, said issuing notice did not mean it was condoning the conduct of the political leaders.

Article Title: 'We all want regime change, anything wrong?' Bhushan attacks government; BJP hits back
Article Text:
"We want regime change, nothing wrong with that": Prashant Bhushan

BJP accuses opposition of legitimising anarchy

NEW DELHI: Senior advocate Prashant Bhushan on Thursday said a change of government would be justified if the ruling dispensation continued to undermine electoral democracy, asserting that citizens had a democratic right to seek regime change. Reacting to his remarks, the BJP accused Rahul Gandhi’s ecosystem of promoting anarchy.Addressing a press conference in New Delhi alongside AISA president Neha Bora and CJP founder Abhijit Dipke, Bhushan rejected the government’s alleged characterisation of the agitation as an opposition-led attempt at regime change.“This government keeps on saying this is the opposition's operation of regime change. We are only appealing to save the electoral democracy in this country. If such barbarism continues, there will definitely be a regime change. We all want a regime change. Is there anything wrong with that? Regime change is a democratic right of every citizen, and creating disaffection against the government is not an offence,” Bhushan said.He further accused the Modi government of undermining electoral democracy and citizens’ fundamental rights.“Such a government cannot continue, which is hell-bent on crushing the electoral democracy in the country and continues to play with the fundamental rights of citizens,” he said.The remarks come amid protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and opposition parties against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.At the same press conference, AISA president Neha Bora expressed solidarity with journalists and criticised the authorities over alleged restrictions on media coverage and the treatment of a woman journalist.“We saw how cameras were snatched from journalists, and they were told that they would not get the camera if they cover this,” Bora said.BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari had accused the march and the opposition’s campaign of seeking to legitimise anarchy rather than pursue democratic resistance. Reacting to a video of Prashant Bhushan’s remarks, Bhandari took to social media platform X, “Prashant Bhushan makes it clear: ‘Yes we want regime change!’ Rahul Gandhi's ecosystem is Anarchic! They are owning up the Anarchy! People of India will defeat Anarchy. Democracy will defeat Rahul Gandhi!” he wrote.
Article Summary: Senior advocate Prashant Bhushan said a change of government would be justified if the ruling dispensation continued to undermine electoral democracy. He said citizens had a democratic right to seek regime change. The BJP accused Rahul Gandhi’s ecosystem of promoting anarchy.

NEW DELHI: BJP Thursday said the SC judgement holding that quota benefits cannot be claimed by converts was "historic", adding it is a "massive blow to the appeasement politics" of Congress and other opposition parties which have sought to provide reservation to Muslims on the basis of religion.While upholding the Madras HC order that a person converting to Islam can't claim reservation under backward class category solely on the basis of conversion, SC also held that a person who professes a religion other than Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism cannot be considered a member of Scheduled Castes (SC).BJP's Gaurav Bhatia lauded the "landmark" ruling, which is a boost to the party's long-held position that Muslims and Christians cannot claim rights accorded to Dalits because of their SC family background and that OBC reservation cannot be provided on the ground of religion."The appeasement politics of 'Congress Jinnah Party' has got a massive blow after the judgement was delivered," he said, noting that Congress govts have tried to give backward quota reservation to Muslims. TMC had done the same in Bengal and SP also advocated a similar quota, he added.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday sought responses from Centre, Delhi govt and Delhi Police on a PIL by NGO ‘Network of Women in Media’ seeking an independent probe, headed by a retired woman judge, into alleged incidents of sexual harassment of women journalists when they were covering the Oct 10 protests.Senior advocate Indira Jaising also mentioned about a woman journalist who was allegedly molested by a senior police officer, who in turn lodged an FIR under SC-ST Act against her for abusing him on caste lines. Such harassment of woman journalists, who form a class by themselves and must be protected while discharging their professional duties, must stop, she said.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta rebutted the charges and said the video purportedly depicting the police officer molesting the woman journalist is an AI-generated clip and that police would respond to the petition after completing investigation into the incident. But a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Joymalya Bagchi directed that the journalist would not be arrested till further orders on the basis of the FIR.Jaising opposed and asked how police, which is accused of molesting a woman journalist, would investigate its officer. It must be handed over to an independent inquiry panel headed by a retired woman judge and comprising a retired woman IPS officer and eminent women representatives from civil society and NGOs.She said she is suggesting names for the composition of the panel from which the court can choose.When the bench allowed Jaising to give names of woman journalists who were allegedly sexually harassed during the protests and names for constituting the proposed panel in two separate sealed covers, Mehta said he opposed Jaising suggesting names for the panel. He said the court may take a call after police file their response to the petition.
Article Summary: Supreme Court seeks responses from Centre, Delhi govt and Delhi Police on a PIL by NGO ‘Network of Women in Media’ seeking an independent probe into alleged incidents of sexual harassment of women journalists when they were covering the Oct 10 protests. Article Title: President Murmu accepts L Murugan’s resignation amid buzz over Union Cabinet reshuffle
Article Text:
President accepted L Murugan's resignation

NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu has accepted the resignation of Union minister of state L Murugan from the Union Council of Ministers, the Rashtrapati Bhavan said on Thursday.The resignation fuelled speculation about an imminent Union Cabinet reshuffle Murugan had resigned as the minister of state for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs on Tuesday, said he wanted to return to Tamil Nadu to strengthen the BJP’s grassroots organisation ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. He also sought permission to relinquish his Rajya Sabha membership.“I requested our Prime Minister to relieve me from the Council of Ministers and the Rajya Sabha because I want to go to Tamil Nadu to strengthen our party,” Murugan said.His exit marks the third resignation by a minister of state after George Kurian and Ravneet Singh Bittu quit in June and July, respectively, following the BJP’s decision not to renominate them for Rajya Sabha elections."The President of India, as advised by the prime minister, has accepted the resignation of Dr L Murugan from the Union Council of Ministers, with immediate effect, under clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution of India," a communique issued by the Rashtrapati Bhavan on Wednesday said.In his letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Murugan described his tenure in the Union government as a privilege.“With humility and grateful heart, I therefore request you to relieve me of my responsibility as MoS and permit me to relinquish my membership of the Rajya Sabha, so that I may dedicate full time to strengthening the party in Tamil Nadu,” he wrote.Murugan said his journey from a family of daily wage labourers to the Union Council of Ministers had been a defining experience.“Now, I wish to return to the grassroots, stand with our 'karyakartas' and dedicate myself full-time to strengthening the BJP in Tamil Nadu ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. Nation First. Party Next. Self Last,” he said.Murugan has been a Rajya Sabha member since September 2021 and was re-elected from Madhya Pradesh in April 2024. His tenure is due to end in April 2030.Several ministers who were not renominated to the Upper House, including Hardeep Singh Puri and BL Verma, continue to hold office. Pankaj Chaudhary and Harsh Malhotra, who were appointed heads of the BJP’s Uttar Pradesh and Delhi units, respectively, have also retained their ministerial responsibilities.
Article Summary: President Droupadi Murmu has accepted the resignation of Union minister of state L Murugan from the Union Council of Ministers. The resignation fuelled speculation about an imminent Union Cabinet reshuffle. He said he wanted to return to Tamil Nadu to strengthen the BJP’s grassroots organisation ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.

Article Title: Govt issues clarification on 'unconditional apology' in SC over internet shutdown
Article Text:
The SC had issued contempt notices to govt on Oct 11 over alleged violation of its earlier order.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Union home minister on Thursday clarified that the unconditional apology submitted by home secretary, the commissioner of police and other officials in their affidavits before the Supreme Court was part of the procedure followed in contempt proceedings.In a statement, the government reacted to the media reports that the Union home secretary Govind Mohan had tendered an unconditional apology to the Supreme Court in response to a contempt notice.It said whenever the Supreme Court issues a contempt notice, the party responding to it is required to begin its affidavit with an unconditional apology, followed by the presentation of other facts and arguments.“This is mandatorily followed in every contempt petition,” the statement said.It added that the affidavits subsequently provided detailed particulars to establish that the actions taken by the government and the police were in accordance with the law and that no case of contempt was made out against them.Mohan, in his affidavit filed late on Wednesday night, said the suspension of cellular internet services within a four-kilometre radius of Raisina Hills from 10 pm on October 9 to 10 pm on October 10 was necessary to prevent a disturbance of public order and maintain peace.He said the Delhi Police 's request for the suspension “was found to be a proportionate measure, having regard to the magnitude of the situation and the need to prevent any disturbance of public order in the national capital.”The Supreme Court had issued contempt notices to Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation chairperson on October 11 over the alleged violation of its earlier order. The court had directed that “internet facilities should function unhindered”.Mohan said the suspension was limited to cellular internet services and did not cover Wi-Fi, broadband or other non-cellular internet services. He argued that suspending internet services for a limited period and within a defined geographical area, subject to statutory safeguards, was a recognised measure to maintain public order in appropriate circumstances.The home secretary also requested the Supreme Court to modify its October 11 order “to the extent necessary to permit the suspension of internet services in situations of necessity, strictly in accordance with law and subject to applicable statutory requirements and safeguards”.
Article Summary: Supreme Court had issued contempt notices to govt on Oct 11 over alleged violation of its earlier order. Govind Mohan tendered an unconditional apology to the Supreme Court in response to a contempt notice. Mohan said the suspension of cellular internet services within a four-kilometre radius of Raisina Hills was necessary to prevent a disturbance of public order.

Article Title: ‘Anarchic, immature’: BJP targets Rahul over anti-CEC protests; claims misconduct with women cop

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Thursday targeted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, describing the Leader of the Opposition (LoP) as “anarchic, immature and irresponsible” and accusing him of undermining constitutional institutions.Addressing a press conference, BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia also alleged that Gandhi had violated the dignity of a woman cop during the protest.“The Congress party and Rahul Gandhi stated that they would stage a protest and approach the Supreme Court . Now, one must ask: what kind of behavior was this?". Bhatia added, "Can 'mobocracy' be allowed to prevail? Can one gather a crowd to pressure the judiciary—an institution that is robust, impartial, and trusted by the people of India?”Bhatia questioned the presence of supporters at the Supreme Court premises, alleging that they had shouted slogans and created a ruckus.“What was the intent behind bringing thousands of supporters to the Supreme Court premises—shouting slogans and creating a ruckus? Can a responsible person—let alone the Leader of the Opposition, or even an ordinary citizen — engage in such conduct? Yet, this is precisely what Rahul Gandhi did,” he said.He further alleged that Gandhi’s conduct was inconsistent with his public messaging on women’s rights, and accused him of inappropriately touching a woman police officer during the protest.“Rahul Gandhi’s ‘smash the patriarchy’ slogan applies only to women in the Gandhi family. During the protest, he inappropriately touched an on-duty woman police officer, compromising her dignity. This amounts to sexual molestation. The court has issued a notice on this petition,” Bhatia said.Additionally, Bhatia described Gandhi as “the very embodiment of anarchy in Indian democracy”, adding that it was “unfortunate” that someone he characterised as “ignorant of the Constitution” held the post of LoP.
Article Summary: The BJP has targeted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Bhatia described the Leader of the Opposition as “anarchic, immature and irresponsible” and accused him of undermining constitutional institutions. Article Title: ‘Stop protecting the VIP’: Ankita Bhandari's parents detained after overnight protest over governor appointment
Article Text:
Congress backs parents as Delhi Police break up overnight dharna

After an overnight vigil at India Gate, a pre-dawn swoop by Delhi Police brought the dharna for “Justice to Ankita Bhandari” to an end. The cops arrived at the protest site at 4 am and took away the wailing parents of Ankita Bhandari, who was murdered in Uttarakhand in 2022.Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and, later, AICC general secretary KC Venugopal visited the protest site on Wednesday evening to express solidarity with the parents. After they left, scores of Congress MPs, MLAs and workers of the Youth Congress and NSUI, among others, joined the dharna. Uttarakhand MLA and Congress office-bearer Qazi Nizamuddin, MPs Pawan Khera, Jothi Mani and Imran Pratapgarhi, Congress spokespersons Supriya Shrinate, Gurdeep Sappal and Ragini Nayak, Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib, NSUI president Vinod Jakhar and Mahila Congress president Alka Lamba, among others, joined the vigil, which continued until early morning before being disrupted by the cops.Videos of the police action went viral, with Chib, Jakhar and others even trying to intercept the bus carrying the detainees.Ankita’s parents arrived from Uttarakhand on Wednesday evening and sat on a dharna along with activist Yogita Bhayana, holding a placard that read, “Stop protecting the VIP”. The continuing controversy over Ankita’s murder received a fresh lease of life with the appointment of BJP leader Dushyant Gautam as governor.The controversy revolves around the “VIP” who had allegedly sought “special service” at the infamous resort then owned by the son of a BJP leader. Ankita resisted the pressure. Her body was found in a canal in 2022, leading to a murder case.In a social media post, the Congress said there were allegations that Gautam was the “VIP” in question. “Narendra Modi has rewarded Gautam with the governorship of Sikkim. The girls and women of the country are watching how Modi and his govt are protecting Gautam.Instead of giving them justice, the entire BJP govt is hellbent on suppressing the voice of Ankita’s parents,” it said.Ankita’s father urged the President of India to put Gautam’s appointment as governor on hold until the CBI inquiry into the issue is completed.Ankita’s parents were taken by the cops to Tilak Marg police station, where they were swiftly joined by Congress leaders protesting the police action against the parents, who were seeking justice for their deceased daughter.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and AICC general secretary KC Venugopal visited the protest site on Wednesday evening. Scores of Congress MPs, MLAs and workers of the Youth Congress and NSUI, among others, joined the dharna.

KOLATHUR: VCK leader Thol Thirumavalavan claimed that DMK leader and former chief minister MK Stalin suffered an electoral defeat in the Kolathur constituency due to mass voter deletions carried out during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Speaking at a joint demonstration organised by the INDIA bloc against the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the implementation of SIR, Thirumavalavan accused the BJP of weaponising the revision process to target political rivals. He alleged that similar electoral roll manipulations had been used against prominent opposition leaders, including West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee and Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan.The protest saw participation from key INDIA bloc partners, including leaders from the Congress, Left parties, MDMK and IUML.Joining the demonstration, TVK leader and minister A Rajmohan reiterated his party’s opposition to the exercise, stating that TVK had consistently opposed the implementation of SIR since its inception.
Article Summary: VCK leader Thol Thirumavalavan claimed that DMK leader and former chief minister MK Stalin suffered an electoral defeat in the Kolathur constituency due to mass voter deletions carried out during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. He accused the BJP of weaponising the revision process to target political rivals.

Article Title: Mumbai Policewoman’s Son Dies After Cement Bench Collapses in Goregaon
Article Text:
Mumbai:





An eight-year-old son of a policewoman died of injuries sustained when a cement bench broke at the Vanrai police quarters, Goregaon East, on Wednesday.Rajvir Kale was the son of Rohini Ghuge-Kale, attached to the Dindoshi Police Station as a constable. The family lived on the seventh floor of building no. 3 at the Vanrai police quarters.Around 9.30 pm on Wednesday, Rajvir was playing on a cement bench in the colony. Benches had been put up for visitors and residents to sit or chat. While playing, the bench suddenly broke, and Rajvir suffered serious injuries. Residents rushed him to the Trauma Care Hospital in Jogeshwari, where he was pronounced dead.Vanrai Police have recorded an accidental death.
Article Summary: Rajvir Kale was the son of Rohini Ghuge-Kale, attached to the Dindoshi Police Station. The family lived on the seventh floor of building no. 3 at the Vanrai police quarters. Rajvir was playing on a cement bench in the colony when it broke.

Article Title: Man held for groping teenage schoolgoer at Masjid railway station in Mumbai
Article Text:
CCTV footage of Masjid railway station was checked besides the area outside railway premises. Police found video grabs of the suspect walking towards Musafirkhana





Mumbai: A teenager was groped at Masjid railway station while she was returning home from school. Within 24 hours of the case being registered, the govt Railway Police (GRP) tracked down the accused and arrested him.The 13-year-old girl had gone to school for an exam on Oct 12. Around 10.45 am, she was heading home after the exam. She was on a foot overbridge on platform 1/2 of the harbour line at Masjid. The 34-year-old accused took cover in the crowds and groped her. He then stalked her to her home in Pydhonie. The girl was terrified and complained to her mother.They approached the Pydhonie police station where a case of molestation was registered. The case was transferred to CSMT GRP for investigation.Teams were formed by senior inspector Sambhaji Katare. CCTV footage of Masjid railway station was checked besides the area outside railway premises. Police found video grabs of the suspect walking towards Musafirkhana.Inquiries were made in the neighbourhood and the CCTV grabs were shown to residents. The accused was identified as Rakesh Gaud (34). Police said he lived in Govandi. He was taken into custody and produced before a court.
Article Summary: The 13-year-old girl had gone to school for an exam on Oct 12. Around 10.45 am, she was heading home after the exam. She was on a foot overbridge on platform 1/2 of the harbour line at Masjid. The accused took cover in the crowds and groped her.

Article Title: Nanded man wanted in intercaste marriage murder case held from Bhopal Central Prison
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A 29-year-old man wanted in a murder case registered by Nanded Rural police in Sept 2024 was arrested from Bhopal Central Jail in Madhya Pradesh on Thursday, where he was allegedly lodged under a false identity in connection with another case.Police said the accused, identified as Palwinder Singh Lachmansingh Chavan, was produced before a Nanded court on Thursday and remanded to police custody till Oct 17.Investigators said Chavan had been absconding since the murder of Shivam Suraj Gaikwad on Sept 20, 2024. Acting on a tip-off, a Nanded police team led by sub-inspector Ravindra Taru verified his presence in Bhopal Central Jail, secured a production warrant and brought him to Nanded.Nanded superintendent of police Neelabh Rohan said the arrest was made as part of a special drive to trace absconding accused involved in serious crimes across the district.Police said Gaikwad was allegedly murdered over his intercaste marriage. As per a complaint filed by his brother, Karan Gaikwad, Chavan and another accused had allegedly threatened Shivam over the marriage. Chavan is accused of attacking Shivam with a sword, causing fatal head and neck injuries.The accused allegedly dumped the body in Godavari river to destroy evidence.Police registered a case under sections 103(1), 238 and 3(5) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with relevant provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. “The co-accused, Devansh alias Devansingh Karansingh Sikkarwar, was arrested and a chargesheet was filed against him in Dec 2024,” an officer said.During the investigation, police found that Chavan had allegedly been using the identity of Balkar Singh, son of Lakshman Singh, while in custody in a govt railway police case registered in Bhopal in 2026.
Article Summary: Palwinder Singh Lachmansingh Chavan was arrested from Bhopal Central Jail. He was allegedly lodged under a false identity in connection with another case. Chavan had been absconding since the murder of Shivam Suraj Gaikwad on Sept 20, 2024.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: Ulhasnagar social activist Haresh Gajwani shot dead outside railway station, 3 arrested
Article Text:
Haresh Gajwani was murdered outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night.





ULHASNAGAR: Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder of social worker Haresh Gajwani, who was shot dead outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night. The suspects have been identified as Avinash Naidu, Vijay Singh and Noor Alam Khan.According to preliminary investigations, Gajwani and Naidu had a long-standing dispute. In 2021, counter-cases were registered against the two sides following a dispute, which allegedly contributed to continuing tensions between Gajwani and the accused.Police said the three suspects were traced and detained with the help of CCTV footage. Investigators are examining the alleged past rivalry, along with other possible motives behind the murder.Gajwani, 54, was allegedly attacked by three assailants who fired two rounds at him before fleeing the scene. Locals and police took him to Central Hospital, where doctors declared him "brought dead".Recently, Gajwani had posted on X, tagging senior officials from various police departments, as well as the chief minister, deputy chief minister and FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe. In his posts, he had highlighted alleged illegal activities in the area and claimed that some police personnel were supporting those involved. He had also expressed fears for his life, warning that the police personnel he had accused would also be responsible if anything happened to him.
Article Summary: Haresh Gajwani, 54, was shot dead outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday. Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder. The suspects have been identified as Avinash Naidu, Vijay Singh and Noor Alam Khan. Investigators are examining the alleged past rivalry, along with other possible motives.

Article Title: Thane Shiv Sena (UBT) leader murder: 2 more arrested near Alibag while fleeing to Goa, total 3
Article Text:
Two additional suspects were arrested in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena division chief Pradeep Purnekar.





THANE: The Thane Crime Branch has arrested two more accused in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) division chief Pradeep alias Balu Purnekar, taking the total number of arrests in the case to three.The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa, according to police sources.The Crime Branch reportedly traced the duo following information obtained during the questioning of suspects detained earlier in the case. Police teams had been searching for the accused after Purnekar was shot and attacked with a sharp-edged weapon at his office in Thane.According to investigators, Yadav allegedly opened fire on Purnekar, while Pawar allegedly attacked him with a sharp weapon. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved in the alleged conspiracy.The two accused are expected to be produced before the Thane Sessions Court on Friday. Police will also attempt to recover the weapons allegedly used in the murder and investigate how the accused obtained them.Earlier, Prakash alias Papya Shinde was arrested in connection with the case. The police have also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by DCP (Crime) Amarsingh Jadhav to conduct a detailed probe into the killing.The investigation is continuing, with police probing the alleged conspiracy, the role of other suspects and the possible involvement of the absconding accused.
Article Summary: The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved.

Article Title: Bawankule to hold Mahayuti rally today over Teachers’ poll

Maharashtra revenue minister and Amravati guardian minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule will hold a workers’ rally at Sant Dnyaneshwar Sanskritik Bhavan today to galvanise Mahayuti workers for the Amravati Division Teachers’ Constituency election.The rally assumes significance as the local BJP cadre has largely stayed away from campaigning for Mahayuti candidate and sitting MLC Kiran Sarnaik of Shiv Sena ( Eknath Shinde faction).The meeting, scheduled for 1 pm, is expected to be attended by functionaries of all constituents of Mahayuti.As per party sources, BJP local functionaries are upset, alleging that Shiv Sena has sidelined them from the campaign. They are fretting and fuming over not being assigned any responsibility or work in the election management.The discontent within the alliance has slowed down campaigning in the division, which comprises five districts.With polling approaching, the BJP leadership is keen to put up a united show. It remains to be seen how Bawankule, who is known for his organisational skills, pacifies the frustrated local cadre and brings unity among Mahayuti constituents for smooth and effective campaigning for Sarnaik.CM Fadnavis, and deputy chief ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar will be present via video conferencing.
Article Summary: Amravati revenue minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule will hold a workers’ rally at Sant Dnyaneshwar Sanskritik Bhavan today. The rally assumes significance as the local BJP cadre has largely stayed away from campaigning for Mahayuti candidate and sitting MLC Kiran Sarnaik of Shiv Sena.

Article Title: Former VAO sentenced to four years in jail for taking bribe of ₹1,000
Article Text:
Krishnagiri

:





A former village administrative officer (VAO) of Thuppuganapalli village in Hosur taluk was sentenced to four years’ rigorous imprisonment in a 2015 bribery case by the principal district court, in Krishnagiri, on Tuesday. The court also imposed a fine of ₹4,000 on him.According to court sources, a village resident had applied to transfer a patta from his mother’s name to his and his father’s names. “M Rajini, who was then village administrative officer, allegedly demanded ₹1,000 to process the application,” said a court official.The complainant approached the directorate of vigilance and anti-corruption (DVAC) in Krishnagiri, which laid a trap. Officials caught Rajini red-handed while accepting ₹1,000 from the complainant. He was arrested and remanded in judicial custody.Following investigation, DVAC filed a chargesheet against Rajini. Principal district judge VR Latha found him guilty and imposed the prison term and fine.
Article Summary: A former village administrative officer (VAO) of Thuppuganapalli village in Hosur taluk was sentenced to four years’ rigorous imprisonment in a 2015 bribery case by the principal district court, in Krishnagiri, on Tuesday. Article Title: Traffic affected on Salem-Madurai National Highway after trailer truck crashes near Rasipuram
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: Traffic was affected for more than an hour on the Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram in Namakkal district on Thursday afternoon after a trailer truck crashed while descending the Andagalur Gate flyover.No casualties or injuries were reported.The truck was carrying about 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. An officer at the Rasipuram police station said the driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover around 1.30pm. The truck hit a streetlight pole on the roadside. “The vehicle partially blocked the road, causing congestion and delays for motorists and commuters,” he said.Vehicles piled up for two kilometres on the NH. The Rasipuram police reached the spot after receiving information, regulated traffic and moved the truck to the roadside.Police registered a case and were investigating the circumstances leading to the crash.

Article Title: CMRL case: Blow to Pinarayi as HC rejects pleas against FIR order
Article Text:
Former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter Veena T, son-in-law and former minister P A Mohamed Riyas

Kochi:





In a setback to former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and his kin, Kerala High Court on Thursday dismissed their applications seeking permission to appeal against a single bench order directing the registration of an FIR against them under the Prevention of Corruption Act in the alleged CMRL-Exalogic payoff case, as well as their appeals against the order.Vijayan, his daughter Veena T, son-in-law and former minister P A Mohamed Riyas, and the other accused had filed the applications as they were not parties to the original petition. With the division bench of Justices K Natarajan and Johnson John rejecting their applications, they cannot appeal against the single bench order as a matter of right. They can, however, challenge the division bench order before Supreme Court.The bench rejected the appellants’ contention that the single bench had passed the impugned order without hearing them, holding that an accused has no legal right to be heard before an FIR is registered in a corruption case. It also held that a preliminary inquiry is not mandatory when information furnished under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) is accompanied by sufficient material disclosing a cognisable offence.The applicants could, however, seek to quash the FIRs by filing appropriate petitions.The case stems from a recommendation by Enforcement Directorate (ED) to the state police chief under Section 66(2) of the PMLA to register a vigilance case against Vijayan and others in the alleged payoff case. Instead, the state govt constituted a special investigation team (SIT) to conduct a preliminary inquiry into ED’s recommendation.On a petition filed by K M Shajahan, a political activist from Thiruvananthapuram, the single bench set aside the govt order constituting the SIT and directed the vigilance director to register an FIR, prompting the applicants to move the division bench.In its judgment, the division bench cited several Supreme Court decisions holding that an accused public servant has no right to be heard before an FIR is registered. It also noted that a preliminary inquiry may be dispensed with when a senior officer receives a detailed, well-reasoned source information report that prima facie discloses a cognisable offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act. The court also noted the state govt’s submission that it had already registered two vigilance cases in compliance with the single bench order.ED had alleged that CMRL paid Rs 3.28 crore to Veena’s now-defunct company, Exalogic Solutions, under the guise of IT consultancy services.
Article Summary: Vijayan, his daughter Veena T, son-in-law and former minister P A Mohamed Riyas, and the other accused had filed the applications as they were not parties to the original petition. With the division bench of Justices K Natarajan and Johnson John rejecting their applications, they cannot appeal against the single bench order as a matter of right.

Article Title: Nedumbassery accident: Suhail Sajeev taken to accident spot for evidence collection
Article Text:
Kochi

:





Police on Thursday took Suhail Sajeev, 19, the key accused in the Nedumbassery car accident that killed three people, to the accident spot on the airport road as part of evidence collection.Suhail remained inside the police vehicle throughout the evidence collection, apparently to avoid a possible public backlash.He was later taken to Courtyard by Marriott in Nedumbassery, one of the three bars that he and the other accused reportedly visited before the accident.According to the police, all four were returned to judicial custody by 5pmon Thursday after the one-day police custody period ended.The state govt had on Wednesday handed over the investigation to Aluva DSP Baiju Paulose. Article Title: Finalise SOP for rehab of children with neurodevelopmental disabilities, Kerala HC tells Union govt
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The high court has urged the Union ministry of social justice and empowerment to finalise the standard operating procedure (SOP) for the care and rehabilitation of children with chronic neurodevelopmental disabilities and ensure its implementation in Keralam.A bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice V M Syam Kumar observed that since the SOP was necessary to support children with chronic neurodevelopmental disabilities, any delay in implementing it could not be countenanced. The observations were made while considering a suo motu case initiated by the court on the need for an effective policy and implementation framework for such children.During the hearing on Wednesday, the central govt placed an office memorandum before the bench stating that it had decided to formulate a comprehensive SOP for the care, rehabilitation and palliative support of children with chronic neurodevelopmental disabilities. For this purpose, it had asked all states and Union Territories to nominate officers to a committee tasked with framing the SOP. So far, nominations have been received from only one concerned department in 14 states, while nominations from the remaining concerned departments are awaited. Keralam has nominated two members. The central govt also submitted that the draft SOP prepared and submitted by the state govt had already been circulated among the authorities in other states.The court observed that any delay in constituting the committee would hold up the finalisation of a national-level SOP and adversely affect children with neurodevelopmental disabilities. The bench accordingly sought the central govt’s response and adjourned the case to Nov 11.
Article Summary: The high court has urged the Union ministry of social justice and empowerment to finalise the standard operating procedure (SOP) for the care and rehabilitation of children with chronic neurodevelopmental disabilities. The observations were made while considering a suo motu case initiated by the court on the need for an effective policy and implementation framework for such children.
